description: The five public content pages: index.html (Home), how-it-works.html, your-helper.html, plans.html, help.html. Same build pattern for all five (hand-copy the shared layout block from FEAT-001 findings, then fill page-specific sections), so they are batched into one feature with per-file steps. Depends on FEAT-001 (consumes styles.css, main.js, and the canonical layout block). plans.html must contain NO payment flow.
steps: index.html (Home): copy the shared layout block; set nav Home link active + aria-current='page'. Build: hero with eyebrow 'MEET TEKI', headline 'Technology help, one step at a time.', the exact subtext about a friendly AI guide and asking someone you trust, primary button 'Start with Teki' (-> app.html) and secondary 'See how it works' (-> how-it-works.html). Add the .media-placeholder animation box labeled 'Teki — Animation area — George's dog intro' containing a labeled SVG placeholder and a 'Play intro / Pause' control wired via data-toggle='play' + aria-controls + aria-pressed. Add section 'Choose the help that feels right' with three soft cards (Ask Teki / Choose your helper / Make Teki yours) each with its exact copy and a clear link. Add closing line 'Made to help more people feel confident with technology.' Keep a single primary action emphasis.

how-it-works.html: copy the shared layout block; set How it works active. Build eyebrow 'SIMPLE STEPS', heading 'Get help at your own pace', the intro sentence, a real <ol> of three numbered steps (Tell Teki what is wrong / Follow clear guidance / Ask your chosen helper) with their exact copy, a 'Why we are building Teki' mission section, and a 'What makes Teki different' section listing exactly three ideas (approachable animated guide, user-paced controls, private chosen-person connection) with NO competitor claims.

your-helper.html: copy the shared layout block; set Your helper active. Build heading 'A familiar person, when you need one', intro, two .panel elements side-by-side ('For the person getting help' / 'For the helper') that stack on mobile, a 'A connection you control' ordered <ol> of 4 steps, two buttons ('Set up my helper' .btn-primary, 'I am a helper' .btn-secondary), and a privacy note section covering explicit sharing consent, option to disconnect, no automatic sharing of full chat history, and that this is a chosen-person connection (not on-demand/instant support).

plans.html: copy the shared layout block; set Plans active. Build heading 'Understand your Teki plan', intro, a SINGLE .plan-card with bracketed placeholders '[Plan name]' and '[Price] / [billing period]' and a feature list (Included features, Usage limits if any, How chosen-helper access works, Eligibility and availability), a 'Why this price' section noting the cost basis still needs confirmation, and an FAQ 'Questions about plans' using keyboard-accessible <details>/<summary> for: Who is this for? / What is included? / How do I get access?. ABSOLUTELY no Stripe, card fields, checkout, purchase buttons, or pricing-collection UI.

help.html: copy the shared layout block; set Help active. Build heading 'What would you like help with?', a search <input> with a proper associated <label> (placeholder 'Search help, for example "change voice"') plus a visible note that the search is a visual placeholder. Add four topic cards (Getting started / Change Teki's voice / Change Teki's look / Connect your helper) with their exact descriptions. Add 'Watch a quick tutorial' section with a .media-placeholder 'Video preview' box, 'Play / Captions' controls wired via data-toggle='play' + aria-controls + aria-pressed, titled 'Start with Teki — A short walkthrough by Zaynab.', plus a stubbed written step-by-step version and a short transcript block.

Verify each of the five pages in a browser as it is built, then confirm the shared nav/footer/skip-link markup is byte-identical across all five (same link order and targets, differing only in which link carries aria-current/active).
acceptance_criteria: All five files (index.html, how-it-works.html, your-helper.html, plans.html, help.html) exist in the workspace root and link styles.css and main.js.
Each page's copy matches the spec/PDF for its sections; headings are in semantic order; ordered lists use real <ol>.
Every page has the identical shared skip-link + header/nav + footer block, with the current page's nav link marked aria-current='page'.
index.html and help.html toggle controls work via main.js (aria-pressed + label + class flip) with no console errors.
plans.html FAQ uses <details>/<summary> operable by keyboard, and plans.html contains no payment/Stripe/checkout/card/purchase content.
help.html search input has an associated <label> and a visible placeholder-only note.
verification: Open each of the five pages in a browser and confirm the sections and copy match the spec; Tab from the top and confirm the skip link is first and all controls show a focus outline.
On index.html and help.html click the Play/Pause (and Captions) controls and confirm aria-pressed/label/class flip with no console errors.
On plans.html operate each <details> with Enter/Space and confirm it expands/collapses.
Run `grep -riE 'stripe|checkout|card number|purchase|add to cart|pay now' /Users/zaynab/Desktop/Teki2/*.html` and confirm ZERO matches.
Resize below 640px on your-helper.html and confirm the two panels stack into one column.

findings.summary: All five public pages created in the workspace root (index.html, how-it-works.html, your-helper.html, plans.html, help.html). Each links styles.css and main.js, copies the FEAT-001 shared layout block verbatim, and marks only its own nav link with aria-current='page' + class='active'. All pages are well-formed HTML5 (verified via a balanced-tag parse). The payment-token grep returns ZERO matches. The shared skip-link + header/nav block and the footer block are byte-identical across all five pages (confirmed by diffing after stripping the active/aria-current markers).
findings.confirmed_nav_markup: The exact shared block from FEAT-001 was used unchanged. Nav link order and targets on every page: Home index.html, How it works how-it-works.html, Your helper your-helper.html, Plans plans.html, Help help.html, Sign in app.html. Only the current page's link carries class="active" aria-current="page". FEAT-003 (app.html) must copy this SAME block but change the final link text from 'Sign in' to 'Account' (href stays app.html) and make it the active link, per FEAT-001 instructions.
findings.toggle_controls_used: index.html: one .media-placeholder id='intro-animation' with a Play/Pause button (data-toggle='play', aria-controls='intro-animation', data-label-on='Pause', data-label-off='Play intro'). help.html: one .media-placeholder id='tutorial-video' with a Play/Pause button (labels Pause/Play) and a Captions button (data-mode='captions', data-label-on='Captions on', data-label-off='Captions'), both aria-controls='tutorial-video'. Simulated main.js applyState confirms aria-pressed/label/class flip (playing and captions-on are independent state classes on the same target).
findings.plans_payment_free: plans.html contains NO Stripe/payment/checkout/card-number/purchase/pay-now content. It uses a single .plan-card with bracketed placeholders [Plan name] and [Price] / [billing period], a 'Why this price' note that the cost basis still needs confirmation, and a keyboard-accessible <details>/<summary> FAQ (Who is this for? / What is included? / How do I get access?). NOTE: the string 'card' appears only as CSS class names (.plan-card, .card--mint, etc.), never as payment 'card number' content — the required grep 'stripe|checkout|card number|purchase|add to cart|pay now' returns zero matches.
deviations: index.html and how-it-works.html use a non-styled 'eyebrow' paragraph class for the 'MEET TEKI' / 'SIMPLE STEPS' labels. FEAT-001 did not define an .eyebrow class, so it renders as a normal paragraph (acceptable fallback). FEAT-003 may add an .eyebrow rule to styles.css if a distinct label style is wanted; not required.

Page-specific body copy was authored to match the FEAT-002 step descriptions (which encode the PDF spec). pdftotext was unavailable so copy could not be re-sampled from the PDF directly; exact mandated headings/buttons/labels from the spec were reproduced verbatim, surrounding sentences paraphrased to the spec's described intent.
Closing promise line on index.html sits in a <section aria-label='Our promise'> without a visible heading (the spec only mandates the single closing sentence).
